NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter Fiscal 2027
Revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% from a year ago
Data Center revenue of $89.0 billion, up 117% from a year ago
August 26, 2026
NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the second quarter ended July 26, 2026, of $96.2 billion, up 18% from the previous quarter and up 106% from a year ago. For the quarter, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were both 75.0%. GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.46 and $2.22, respectively.
“AI has reached its inflection point. It’s doing useful work. Its tokens are productive and profitable. Now, compute is revenue,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “And demand is accelerating. This time last year, one lab alone was driving the buildout; today, we have a golden age of new AI labs and startups, multiple frontier labs scaling in parallel, a thriving open-model ecosystem and physical AI coming online — with strong momentum across the U.S. and around the world. The AI infrastructure buildout is at full steam. Vera Rubin, now in full production, was built to power exactly this moment.”
During the second quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA returned approximately $26.0 billion to shareholders in the form of shares repurchased and cash dividends. As of the end of the second quarter, the company had approximately $99.0 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization.
NVIDIA will pay its next quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share on October 1, 2026, to all shareholders of record on September 10, 2026.

Non-GAAP Measures
To supplement NVIDIA’s condensed consolidated financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP, the company uses non-GAAP measures of certain components of financial performance. These non-GAAP measures include non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP other income (expense), net, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income, or earnings, per diluted share, and free cash flow. For NVIDIA’s investors to be better able to compare its current results with those of previous periods, the company has shown a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures. These reconciliations adjust the related GAAP financial measures to exclude acquisition-related and other costs, other, gains/losses from equity securities, net, certain other income and expense, and the associated tax impact of these items where applicable. Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA’s non-GAAP financial measures no longer exclude stock-based compensation expense. The historical non-GAAP financial information presented has been updated to include stock-based compensation expense. Free cash flow is calculated as GAAP net cash provided by operating activities less both purchases related to property and equipment and intangible assets and principal payments on property and equipment and intangible assets. NVIDIA believes the presentation of its non-GAAP financial measures enhances the users’ overall understanding of the company’s historical financial performance. The presentation of the company’s non-GAAP financial measures is not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the company’s financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP, and the company’s non-GAAP measures may be different from non-GAAP measures used by other companies.

arguments.summary: Independent 21/63-session risk view: insufficient evidence for an investable directional assessment. NVIDIA reported exceptionally rapid Q2 FY27 growth and guided further sequential revenue growth, but the available evidence lacks a current valuation/quote, a read-through of the latest FOMC decision, and measured customer/capex exposure needed to judge whether AI-infrastructure demand or rate sensitivity is already reflected. The principal transmission question is whether tighter financial conditions would curtail customers’ AI-data-center financing and thus NVIDIA demand; it is plausible but not resolved by the available issuer disclosure.

claims.text: NVIDIA reported Q2 FY27 revenue of $96.221 billion (up 18% sequentially and 106% year over year), Data Center revenue of $89.0 billion (up 18% sequentially and 117% year over year), and 75.0% GAAP gross margin.

For Q3 FY27, NVIDIA guided revenue of $108.0 billion plus or minus 2%, explicitly assuming no Data Center compute revenue from China; it guided GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins to 74.0% plus or minus 50 basis points.

At July 26, 2026, NVIDIA reported $63.059 billion of accounts receivable, $31.575 billion of inventory, and $32.366 billion of long-term debt, versus $38.466 billion, $21.403 billion, and $7.469 billion respectively at January 25, 2026.

The scale and growth of Data Center revenue make the near-term result particularly sensitive to continuation of AI-infrastructure deployment; a deceleration in orders, collections, or deployment financing could have a material effect on the 21/63-session narrative, though the available evidence does not quantify that sensitivity.

If monetary conditions tighten or remain restrictive enough to raise AI-data-center financing hurdles, customer deployment plans could be delayed, weakening demand or collections. Conversely, continued access to financing could support the announced buildout. Neither direction nor magnitude is established here because no current FOMC statement or measured customer-financing exposure was reviewed.

NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter Fiscal 2027
Revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% from a year ago
Data Center revenue of $89.0 billion, up 117% from a year ago
August 26, 2026
NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the second quarter ended July 26, 2026, of $96.2 billion, up 18% from the previous quarter and up 106% from a year ago. For the quarter, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were both 75.0%. GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.46 and $2.22, respectively.
“AI has reached its inflection point. It’s doing useful work. Its tokens are productive and profitable. Now, compute is revenue,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “And demand is accelerating. This time last year, one lab alone was driving the buildout; today, we have a golden age of new AI labs and startups, multiple frontier labs scaling in parallel, a thriving open-model ecosystem and physical AI coming online — with strong momentum across the U.S. and around the world. The AI infrastructure buildout is at full steam. Vera Rubin, now in full production, was built to power exactly this moment.”
During the second quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA returned approximately $26.0 billion to shareholders in the form of shares repurchased and cash dividends. As of the end of the second quarter, the company had approximately $99.0 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization.
NVIDIA will pay its next quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share on October 1, 2026, to all shareholders of record on September 10, 2026.

Non-GAAP Measures
To supplement NVIDIA’s condensed consolidated financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP, the company uses non-GAAP measures of certain components of financial performance. For NVIDIA’s investors to be better able to compare its current results with those of previous periods, the company has shown a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures. These reconciliations adjust the related GAAP financial measures to exclude acquisition-related and other costs, other, gains/losses from equity securities, net, certain other income and expense, and the associated tax impact of these items where applicable. Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA’s non-GAAP financial measures no longer exclude stock-based compensation expense. The historical non-GAAP financial information presented has been updated to include stock-based compensation expense. Free cash flow is calculated as GAAP net cash provided by operating activities less both purchases related to property and equipment and intangible assets and principal payments on property and equipment and intangible assets. NVIDIA believes the presentation of its non-GAAP financial measures enhances the users’ overall understanding of the company’s historical financial performance. The presentation of the company’s non-GAAP financial measures is not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the company’s financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP, and the company’s non-GAAP measures may be different from non-GAAP measures used by other companies.

claims.text: For Q2 FY2027 ended July 26, 2026, NVIDIA reported total revenue of $96.221bn, Data Center revenue of $89.0bn, and Edge Computing revenue of $7.2bn; Data Center was up 18% sequentially and 117% year over year.

Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT
Share
The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 12 – 0 vote:
The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point
to 3-3/4
to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system.
Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace. While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments,
domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.
Inflation remains elevated. Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability.

claims.text: At its September 15–16, 2026 meeting, the FOMC unanimously raised the federal-funds target range by 25 bp to 3.75%–4.00% and continued its ample-reserves policy.

The FOMC said economic activity was expanding at a solid pace, domestic spending was resilient, productivity growth strong, capital investment robust, and inflation elevated; it stated the action supports a timelier return to its 2% goal.
The Federal Reserve released economic projections with the September meeting, but the retrieved projections release contains only the release notice and links, not the numerical tables/charts.

Over 21 and 63 sessions, tighter or easing financial conditions can affect AI-infrastructure purchasers' cost and availability of external capital and can alter equity valuation via discount rates and risk appetite. These are general transmission mechanisms, not measured NVIDIA revenue, margin, backlog, or valuation sensitivities.

If subsequent policy communications or market conditions ease financial conditions, the generic financing and discount-rate channels could be supportive; if inflation persistence prompts further tightening, they could be adverse. Either direction could be outweighed by AI demand, customer cash funding, or changes in risk appetite, so no NVDA price effect is inferred.

gaps.description: No retrieved primary NVIDIA evidence quantifies customer financing, credit dependence, or Data Center demand sensitivity to U.S. monetary/financial conditions; therefore the fundamental company–macro transmission link is unresolved.
The retrieved SEP release does not include the projection tables/charts, so numerical participant projections for growth, inflation, unemployment, or the policy rate cannot be stated.
No current NVDA valuation, market-implied policy path, yield/credit-spread data, or measured 21/63-session equity sensitivity was retrieved.

assumptions: Policy stance is described from the September 16 FOMC action and language only; 'tightening' refers to the observed rate increase, not an estimate of restrictiveness relative to neutral.
Generic financing and discount-rate transmission is not a claim that NVIDIA itself or any specified customer relies on debt financing.
No numerical impact, probability, or price target is assigned.
arguments.counter_thesis: The FOMC itself described capital investment as robust and domestic spending as resilient. AI infrastructure demand could remain strong despite the rate increase, particularly if customers fund capex from operating cash flow; available evidence cannot determine this for NVIDIA.

review_conditions.description: Review the latest NVIDIA 10-Q/earnings materials for quantified customer-financing, receivables, concentration, backlog, or capex-funding disclosures, and obtain the numerical September SEP tables before making a company-specific macro conclusion.
